hero.title: Export Customs Clearance
hero.description: Winz supports exporters, freight forwarders, and logistics companies with AES filing, document checks, dual-use screening, origin evidence, and proof-of-exit follow-up.
hero.intro1: Export customs clearance in Belgium requires an electronic declaration, a valid EORI number, accurate documents, and proof that the goods left the EU. The procedure applies when Union goods leave Belgium for a non-EU destination.
hero.intro2: Winz does not provide transport services. Winz helps businesses complete customs clearance Belgium for air freight, road freight, and container shipments.

process.title: Five Export Clearance Stages
process.description: The Belgian export process normally covers declaration filing, customs release, movement to the exit point, physical departure, and exit confirmation.

stages.title: Stage 1 — AES Export Declaration
stages.desc: Winz submits the electronic export declaration through Belgium's Automated Export System (AES) before goods leave the EU. The declaration includes exporter, consignee, EORI, product, value, currency, destination, Incoterm, packaging, weight, procedure, and transport details.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Export Control Checks
stages.desc: EU export regulations and dual-use controls require authorisation for certain goods. Winz reviews classification, technical specifications, destination, consignee, and intended use for export-control risks.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Origin and Trade Documents
stages.desc: Winz reviews origin evidence against destination requirements and applicable trade agreements. Preferential duty requires goods to meet product-specific origin rules, using evidence like EUR.1 certificates or REX registration.

stages.title: Stage 4 — Customs Office of Exit
stages.desc: The customs office of export processes and releases the declaration. The office of exit supervises departure and returns the exit result. These offices may be in different EU countries.

stages.title: Stage 5 — Proof of Exit
stages.desc: Proof of exit confirms that goods left the EU and supports export records and VAT treatment. Winz monitors export status and follows up on missing confirmation.

documents.title: Export Documents
documents.description: Export documents support customs, tax, commercial, and transport requirements. Missing or inconsistent details can delay clearance and increase audit risk.

items.purpose: Confirms parties, goods, value, currency, and Incoterm
Lists contents, packages, weights, and dimensions

items.doc: CMR, bill of lading, or airway bill
items.purpose: Records road, sea, or air shipment details

documents.note: Road shipments require a CMR consignment note road freight as the legally required transport document on all cross-border truck departures from Belgium.

document_checks.title: Export Document Checks
document_checks.p1: Winz checks export documents before filing to reduce customs delays, VAT exposure, and compliance errors.
document_checks.p2: Each file is compared with the commercial invoice, packing list, export declaration data, transport document, origin evidence, and licence requirements. The review can identify incorrect HS codes, missing EORI numbers, value differences, and incomplete destination details.
document_checks.p3: The declaration data must reflect the commercial transaction and physical shipment. Customs may stop the filing when the package counts, weights, values, or goods descriptions do not match.
document_checks.p4: Proof of exit also needs attention. Belgian exporters require reliable export evidence to support the VAT treatment of goods sold outside the EU.

direct_indirect.title: Direct and Indirect Exports
direct_indirect.p1: A direct export leaves the EU through the same member state where the export declaration is processed. For example, goods declared in Belgium may leave through the Port of Antwerp.
direct_indirect.p2: An indirect export leaves through another EU member state. A Belgian declaration may therefore close after the goods depart through Rotterdam, Hamburg, Amsterdam Airport Schiphol, or another EU exit point.
direct_indirect.p3: Indirect exports require accurate communication between the office of export and office of exit. The MRN must remain connected to the goods throughout the movement.
direct_indirect.p4: Errors in the exit reference, carrier reporting, or arrival message can delay closure. Exporters should check the movement status instead of assuming that physical departure automatically closes the declaration.

definitions.title: Declaration, EAD, MRN, and Exit Proof
definitions.p1: An export declaration is the electronic customs filing used to place Union goods under the export procedure.
definitions.p2: The MRN is the unique reference assigned to the accepted customs movement. It allows customs offices and authorised operators to identify and track the filing.
definitions.p3: The Export Accompanying Document contains key declaration and MRN information. Its use depends on the export movement and the digital process followed by the customs offices and operators.
definitions.p4: Proof of exit is the confirmation that the goods left the EU customs territory.
definitions.p5: These records serve different purposes. The declaration starts the procedure. The MRN identifies the movement. The EAD supports movement control. The exit result closes the export process and supports the exporter's records.

exporter_purposes.title: Exporter for Customs Purposes
exporter_purposes.p1: The exporter is the party identified as responsible for the export under EU customs rules.
exporter_purposes.p2: For a business transaction, the exporter normally needs to be established in the EU customs territory. The business must also have the power to determine, and must have determined, that the goods will leave the EU.
exporter_purposes.p3: Where those conditions do not apply, an EU-established party to the export contract may qualify under the customs definition. A non-EU business cannot simply appear as the exporter because it owns or sells the goods. Contractual arrangements must identify an eligible EU-established exporter.
exporter_purposes.p4: Incoterms such as EXW, FOB, CIF, and DDP affect commercial costs, risks, and responsibilities. They do not independently determine who qualifies as the exporter under customs law.
exporter_purposes.p5: The exporter and customs declarant can also be different parties. A customs representative may file directly in the exporter's name or indirectly in its own name, depending on the agreed representation and legal requirements.

delays.title: Common Export Delays
delays.p1: Belgian export delays usually result from declaration errors, missing licences, customs controls, or unclosed exit movements.
items: Missing a dual-use or export licence
Carrier delay in reporting arrival or departure
Customs inspection at export or exit

cost_factors.title: Export Clearance Cost Factors
cost_factors.p1: Export clearance costs depend on declaration type, product controls, document requirements, destination, and customs follow-up level.
items: Declaration type — standard export, re-export, and transit-linked exports each follow different procedures
Product type — chemicals, electronics, machinery, and controlled goods require additional checks
Origin evidence — EUR.1, statements on origin, and A.TR each require different review
Transport context — road, air, and container exports use different movement and exit documents
Licence requirements — controlled goods need technical checks and authorisation support
Customs inspection — scanning or physical examination increases coordination work
Exit follow-up — an open movement may require status checks and alternative proof
cost_factors.p2: Winz confirms required customs work before filing so exporters know which declarations, documents, and checks apply.
